svg.title: Geant4 and Geant4-DNA: user definitions and simulation flow
svg.desc: Generic reference: the minimal user classes needed to run a Geant4 simulation, the kernel application states, the three Geant4-DNA stages of one event (physical, pre-chemical, chemical) with the user hooks, and the ready-made or custom DNA physics and chemistry choices.
svg.text: Geant4 and Geant4-DNA: what you define and how a simulation flows
Generic reference, not tied to one project. Read A (what you write), B (kernel states), C (one event through the three DNA stages), D (physics and chemistry choices).
A. What you write: the minimum for any simulation
then G4UImanager: run a macro or open a GUI.
The factory picks Serial, MT or Tasking.
Which particles, processes and models exist.
For Geant4-DNA it holds two constructors:
Construct() builds and returns the world
in the volume where particles are tracked.
what the kernel does between your commands
run ends: back to Idle, /run/beamOn can be issued again
C. One event in Geant4-DNA: three stages
the kernel drives every step, your hooks (orange) are optional except the generator
The run manager loops over the events.
G4ParticleGun puts a primary e- on
The e- is tracked step by step with the
G4DNA processes of the chosen physics
the dissociation channels of the chemistry
placed as molecule tracks for the
Physical tracks are done, the stack is
dt, species diffuse and react through the
Time-step hooks fire at every step.
Species counters and scorers hold the
chemical: ps up to the scheduler EndTime (e.g. 1 us)
D. Choose or write the DNA physics and chemistry
Each option is a different set of DNA models
Used as physical stage in the PhysicsList.
Reference wiring: examples/extended/medical/dna/chem6. Its PhysicsList holds G4EmDNAPhysics_option2 + G4EmDNAChemistry_option3 and forwards ConstructParticle() / ConstructProcess() to both;
